There are two doors into the vendor register, and which one you use depends on who you are. Anyone who can see the register can request a vendor; the third-party risk team can add one directly and decides every request. This page covers all three tasks.

## Request a vendor

If you can see the vendor register you can ask for a new vendor. You are not creating one: the third-party risk team reviews every request.

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the request form">

Click **Request vendor** in the header of **Vendors**.

</Step>
<Step title="Describe what you need">

Give the vendor's name, your department, what you want them to do, and how urgent it is. Under **Intended use**, include any data they would see. **Urgency** is Low (no fixed date), Normal, or High (blocked without it).

</Step>
<Step title="Submit">

Click **Submit request**. Verity checks the name against the register. If it looks like a vendor you already use, the dialog stays open and shows you which, before anyone reviews it. Your request is still submitted, so close the dialog with **Done**.

</Step>
</Steps>

<Screenshot name="dialog-request-vendor" alt="The Request a vendor dialog with fields for the vendor name, your department, urgency and intended use" />

The request lands in **Vendors > Intake**. Nothing is in the register yet.

## Add a vendor directly

If you run third-party risk and have permission to manage vendors, you can skip the request and add the vendor yourself.

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the form">

Click **Add vendor**.

</Step>
<Step title="Describe the organisation">

Fill in the name, type, industry, website and business unit. **Type** is Vendor, Supplier, Contractor or Partner. Add the **Services provided** if you know them.

</Step>
<Step title="Record the data they touch">

Record what data they touch: whether they hold personal data, the classification, where it lives, and which systems are in scope.

</Step>
<Step title="Name the owners">

Name the three owners: business, security and relationship.

</Step>
<Step title="Name the first engagement">

Name the **first engagement**. This is what gets tiered. You can add it later, but tiering cannot start without one.

</Step>
<Step title="Save">

Click **Add vendor**.

</Step>
</Steps>

<Screenshot name="dialog-add-vendor" alt="The Add vendor dialog with the name, type, industry, website, business unit and services, a data section for personal data, classification, location and systems in scope, and the business, security and relationship owners with the first engagement" />

## Decide an intake request

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the queue">

Go to **Vendors > Intake**. Pending requests sort first, and the tab carries a count of what is waiting. Switch between **Pending**, **Approved**, **Declined** and **All** to see past decisions.

</Step>
<Step title="Read the request">

Read the request: who asked, their urgency, what they want the vendor for and the data it would see. If screening flagged possible duplicates, the matching vendors are listed with links under **Already in the register**. Approving creates a duplicate unless they are different organisations.

</Step>
<Step title="Approve it">

**Approve and create** creates the vendor and its first engagement and takes you to it.

</Step>
<Step title="Or decline it">

**Decline** requires a reason. Nothing is created, the reason is kept, and the requester sees it.

</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warning" title="Before you click">

You cannot decide the same request twice, and a decline cannot be undone. Declining keeps the reason forever. If circumstances change, raise a new request rather than trying to revive a declined one, so the history shows both decisions.

</Callout>

<Screenshot name="vendors-intake" alt="The Intake tab listing pending requests with their urgency and screening status, a warning that one request matches a vendor already in the register, and Approve and create and Decline buttons" />

Deciding a request needs permission to manage vendors. Without it, you can read the queue but the buttons are replaced by a note saying who can decide.

## After approval

Approving takes you to the new vendor's record. Its **Overview** tab shows what the vendor does for you, the data you share, its engagements, and the owners, key dates and contacts. The next step is to tier the first engagement.

<Screenshot name="vendor-detail" alt="A vendor record's Overview tab showing what the vendor does, the data shared, the engagements with their tier and status, and panels for ownership, key dates and contacts" />

The Intake tab also holds the **Shadow IT** list of apps found in use that never came through a request. See [Triage shadow IT](/docs/vendors/contracts-monitoring-offboarding/#triage-shadow-it).
